21: PELAGÉYA EGÓROVNA. Girls, sing a song for him.
20: GORDÉY KÁRPYCH. Come now and have a drink. KÓRSHUNOV. All right, Gordéy Kárpych, give me something to drink. And you girls, sing a song in my honor—I love to have respect shown me.
19: Enter PELAGÉYA EGÓROVNA, and after her, ARÍNA and EGÓRUSHKA with wine and glasses. The same with PELAGÉYA EGÓROVNA, ARÍNA, and EGÓRUSHKA
18: KÓRSHUNOV. I gave it to you, and I won't take it back! He, he, he!
17: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. But I don't want it. Give it to whomever you like. [ Takes it off and returns it.
16: KÓRSHUNOV. That's all right; it's no loss to me—it won't ruin me.
15: KÓRSHUNOV. What a hand! He, he, he! Like velvet! [ Strokes her hand, and then puts on a diamond ring. LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. [ Freeing her hand ] Oh, let me go! I don't want it; I don't want it!
14: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. [ Gives her hand ] Oh, good heavens!
13: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA sits down. KÓRSHUNOV. You don't want to sit by the old man? Give me your hand, young lady; I will kiss it.
12: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. To mother! GORDÉY KÁRPYCH. Wait! She'll come here.
11: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. [ Rising ] I don't need your money. GORDÉY KÁRPYCH. Lyubóv, where are you going?
10: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. Why shouldn't I like you? KÓRSHUNOV. Why? You like some one else, that's why. But you will come to love me! I'm a good man—a jolly man, he, he, he!
9: MÁSHA. But they are charming! LÍZA. And in such good taste!
8: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. Oh, they're earrings! I thank you humbly. ANNA IVÁNOVNA. Show them to us.
7: KÓRSHUNOV. [ Seats himself near LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA] I'm not like you, Lyubóv Gordéyevna; you didn't even want to kiss me, he, he, he! And I've brought you a little present. LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. You needn't have taken the trouble.
6: MÍTYA, GÚSLIN and RAZLYULYÁYEV go out . GORDÉY KÁRPYCH, KÓRSHUNOV, LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA, ANNA IVÁNOVNA, MÁSHA, LÍZA and girls .
5: LÍZA. Well, there's nothing to be said; I must say it's a treat! GORDÉY KÁRPYCH. [ Going up to MÍTYA] Why are you here? Is this your place? "The crow has flown into the lofty palace!"
4: ANNA IVÁNOVNA. I suppose so! I'm not proud. MÁSHA. Oh, how embarrassing!
3: LYUBÓV GORDÉYEVNA. If my father wants me to. [ They exchange kisses . KÓRSHUNOV. Well now, every one of them, right down the line.
2: GORDÉY KÁRPYCH. You're welcome to do so; don't stand on ceremony. KÓRSHUNOV. Will you give me a kiss, young lady?
1: ANNA IVÁNOVNA. Why be so affectionate? KÓRSHUNOV. Gordéy Kárpych, may I kiss your daughter? And I must confess—he, he—I'm fond of this sort of thing. Yes, well, who doesn't like it! He, he!
0: ANNA IVÁNOVNA. Be seated; you'll be our guest. KÓRSHUNOV. You're pretty chilly to the old man! It's Christmas time now, and I suppose we may exchange kisses.
